sentences.text: Bacteroides xylanisolvens was described from xylanolytic, Gram-negative, anaerobic rods isolated from human faecal samples during a study of the xylan-degrading community of the gut.
The isolates degraded different types of xylan and grew on a variety of carbohydrates but, unlike most other Bacteroides species from the human gut, could not degrade starch.
A culturomics study reported that this species, together with Bacteroides zhangwenhongii and Bacteroides difficilis, can degrade the food additive carrageenan.
In cell-culture work, human gut isolates of Bacteroides xylanisolvens and Bacteroides cellulosilyticus were reported to reduce inflammation in Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells.
